newsitem.title: UK: UK June s/a mortgage lending rises 905 mln stg-BBA.
newsitem.headline: UK June s/a mortgage lending rises 905 mln stg-BBA.

text.p: Net lending to house buyers by Britain's major banks rose by a seasonally adjusted 905 million stg in June, up nearly 11 percent from the May figure of 818 million and well above the recent monthly average, the British Bankers' Association said on Monday.
The BBA said the rise was the highest since the series began four years ago.

Unadjusted gross loans totalled 2.861 billion stg in June, some 13.0 percent higher than the May figure of 2.526 billion. In June 1996, there was a marginal fall in gross lending. This series is not seasonally adjusted.
The number of net new approvals were only slightly weaker than in May. There were 49,972 loans approved, while their value eased to 2.807 billion stg from 2.913 billion in May.

In June last year, there was a similar picture in the number of approvals though their average value at that time was rising. By contrast this June saw the second successive fall in the average approval value to 56,200 stg, some 2.0 percent lower than a year earlier.

The BBA also said that during the second quarter of the year, fixed rate mortgages were estimated to have accounted for around 45 percent of all gross lending, compared with 34 percent in the first quarter and 25 percent a year earlier.
BBA director General Tim Sweeney said that overall the figures continued to reflect the buoyant state of the housing market.
"Net lending in June rose significantly to be some 17 percent above the recent average and gross lending reached a new monthly peak of 2.9 billion stg," he said.

"In April and May, there was strong demand for approvals particularly on fixed-rate terms, reflecting borrowers' uncertainty over interest rates and fears over possible budget measures affecting the housing market. This demand may have been expect to decline in June but in the event the approvals data for the month were almost as strong as in May.
"Overall, the June figures show no sign of the banks' mortgage business levelling off, and indeed may represent increasing market share," he said.
